analysis.investment_thesis: Desco Infratech is a sub-₹125 Cr microcap civil construction contractor earning a dismal 0.26% ROE — effectively destroying capital. Invert: a business earning less than a savings account at this scale in a working-capital-heavy, cyclical, contract-dependent industry is exactly what I tell people to avoid.
key_strengths: Promoter holding 58.31% indicates skin in the game
Exposure to growing infrastructure themes (CGD, renewables, water)
P/E of 10.4 is not optically expensive
key_risks: ROE of 0.26% is catastrophic — no real earnings power
EPC/civil construction is low-moat, working-capital-intensive, receivables-heavy
Recently listed microcap (2011 incorp., just listed) with no public track record
red_flags: ROE 0.26% makes the reported P/E of 10.4 essentially meaningless — denominator is near zero
Zero FII and negligible (2.2%) DII participation — no institutional due-diligence validation
Tiny ₹124 Cr market cap in a capital-intensive contracting business — scale disadvantage vs L&T/KEC/Kalpataru
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Apply inversion: what kills contractors? Negative operating cash flow, receivable blowups, cost overruns on fixed-price contracts, over-leverage to fund working capital, and client concentration. An ROE of 0.26% already tells me this business is not earning its cost of capital — it is worth less than the equity on its books in any rational DCF. A P/E of 10 on near-zero E is a statistical artifact, not a bargain. City Gas Distribution and renewables EPC sound exciting, but the economics accrue to the asset owners (GAIL, Adani Gas, NTPC), not to the sub-contractor laying pipes.

In Munger's framework, this fails the first filter — "understand the business and its durable advantage." There is no moat in civil construction at ₹124 Cr scale; pricing power is nil, competitive bidding compresses margins, and a single delayed receivable can wipe out a year's earnings. Combined with zero institutional ownership and a very recent listing, this is a speculative microcap, not an investment. I would put it in the "too hard / too risky" pile and move on. Pass.
